### 6. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-011`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

For years, jeepneys in a busy town in Pampanga stopped wherever a passenger raised a hand. Drivers competed for riders, and the main road was often blocked by vehicles halting in the middle of traffic. Last year, the town marked twelve loading bays along the route and ruled that jeepneys may stop only at these bays. At first, many commuters complained that they now had to walk farther. Drivers, too, worried that they would lose passengers to tricycles. Six months later, the picture is different. Travel time on the main road during rush hour has fallen by about a third, according to the town's traffic office. Drivers say they make more trips each day, which makes up for the riders they lose. Commuters have also adjusted; many now leave home a few minutes earlier to reach a bay. The council plans to add roofs and benches at the busiest bays, since standing in the sun or rain was the most common complaint in a recent survey.

What is the passage mainly about?

- (A) How traffic offices measure travel time
- (B) How fixed loading bays changed jeepney travel in a town
- (C) Why commuters prefer tricycles to jeepneys
- (D) The history of public transport in the Philippines

### 9. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-021`  (both, easy, 45 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

When the provincial library extended its hours to 8 p.m. on weekdays, the staff expected students to fill the reading room. Instead, the largest new group turned out to be working adults. Many were employees who had never been able to visit because the library used to close at five. Some came to read newspapers; others used the computers to apply for jobs or to file online forms. A few brought their children to do homework while they read nearby. The librarian noticed that the evening visitors asked for different help than daytime users. Students usually wanted reference books, but adults often needed help with government websites. In response, the library trained two staff members to guide visitors through common online services, such as renewing documents and checking benefit records. The evening program costs the province little, since it uses the same building and only shifts staff schedules. The librarian now hopes to open on Saturday afternoons, when, she believes, even more families could come together.

According to the passage, who made up the largest new group of evening visitors?

- (A) Students
- (B) Working adults
- (C) Children doing homework
- (D) Retired teachers

### 12. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-031`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Fishermen in a coastal village in Antique were at first unhappy when the town declared part of their bay a fish sanctuary. No one may fish inside the marked zone, which covers about a tenth of the bay. The fishermen feared that they would catch less, since the sanctuary included some of their favorite spots. The town's agriculture office explained that fish breed safely inside the zone and later swim out into the open waters. To show this, the office and the fishermen's association recorded catches for three years. In the first year, catches outside the sanctuary stayed about the same. By the third year, however, the average daily catch had grown noticeably, and larger fish of several kinds had returned. Some fishermen now serve as volunteer guards, reporting boats that enter the zone at night. The association says that the sanctuary works only because the villagers themselves agreed to protect it, and it warns that the gains could vanish if the rule is not enforced.

Which title best fits the passage?

- (A) A Sanctuary That Fishermen Learned to Protect
- (B) Why Fishermen Oppose New Rules
- (C) How to Catch Larger Fish at Night
- (D) The Fish of Antique

### 15. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-041`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

The rural health unit in a mountain town used to give out numbered stubs at seven in the morning. Patients who lived far away often arrived after all the stubs were gone and had to return the next day. To solve this, the unit began accepting appointments by text message. A patient sends his or her name and reason for the visit, and the unit replies with a time. Walk-in patients are still served, but appointments fill most of the morning. The doctor reports that the waiting area is now calmer, and nurses spend less time managing the line. Not everyone has benefited equally, however. Some older residents do not own phones, and a few cannot read text messages. For them, barangay health workers send messages on their behalf during home visits. The unit is now counting how many patients still arrive without appointments, to decide whether to reserve more hours for walk-ins.

What is the main idea of the passage?

- (A) Every patient now has an appointment
- (B) Mountain towns lack doctors
- (C) Barangay health workers make home visits
- (D) Text-message appointments improved the clinic's service, though some residents still need help

### 18. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-051`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

When a city treasurer's office moved to a new building, employees found the rooms bright but bare. A clerk suggested placing a few potted plants near the windows, and the office manager agreed to try it for three months. Employees took turns watering the plants, and some brought cuttings from home. The manager did not expect much, but she noticed changes. Staff spent more of their breaks talking near the windows instead of at their desks, and a few said they felt less tired by the afternoon. The plants also became a topic that brought together employees from different sections who had seldom spoken before. When the trial ended, the office voted to keep the plants and to add more. The manager is careful not to claim too much. She says the plants did not make anyone work faster, but they made the office a friendlier place to spend eight hours a day.

What is the passage mainly about?

- (A) The design of the city's new buildings
- (B) How a few plants made a new office friendlier
- (C) Why employees work faster near windows
- (D) How to grow plants from cuttings

### 21. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-061`  (both, easy, 45 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

A town in Quezon used to issue senior citizen IDs only at the municipal hall, which was open on weekdays. The ID gives older residents discounts on medicines, fares and other basic needs, so delays in getting one cost them money. Many older residents in far barangays had to pay for a tricycle ride and sometimes come back twice because of missing documents. This year, the town's social welfare office began a monthly outreach. A small team visits one barangay each week with a laptop, a camera and a printer. Before each visit, barangay officials post a list of the documents applicants should bring. Residents who lack a birth certificate can present other proof of age, such as a baptismal certificate or a voter's ID. The team issues most IDs on the spot. Those with incomplete papers receive a checklist and can finish their applications at the next visit. The office reports that it issued more IDs in the first four months of the program than in the whole of last year.

According to the passage, what do barangay officials do before each visit?

- (A) Collect fees from applicants
- (B) Print the IDs in advance
- (C) Drive residents to the municipal hall
- (D) Post a list of the documents applicants should bring

### 24. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-071`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Every June, a public elementary school in Samar holds a typhoon drill before the rainy season begins. The drill takes about an hour and involves every pupil, teacher and staff member on campus. Teachers lead pupils from the classrooms to the school's evacuation hall, a concrete building on higher ground. Each class has an assigned place in the hall, marked with its section name. Parents are invited to watch so that they know where to pick up their children during a real storm. After the drill, the principal meets with teachers to discuss problems. Last year, they found that one stairway was too narrow for two classes at once, so they changed the exit order. This year, they added a practice of checking the attendance list inside the hall. The principal says the drill used to feel like a formality. Since a strong typhoon hit the town three years ago, however, teachers and parents take it seriously, and attendance at the drill is almost complete.

What is the passage mainly about?

- (A) How a school prepares for typhoons and improves its drill each year
- (B) How strong typhoons damage schools
- (C) Why the evacuation hall is made of concrete
- (D) Why parents pick up their children late

### 27. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-081`  (both, easy, 45 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Shoppers in a public market in Cavite had long suspected that some scales were inaccurate. A few grams missing from each kilo may seem small, but for a family buying fish every day, the losses add up over a month. In response, the market administrator set up a "timbangan ng bayan," a public scale near the entrance that anyone can use for free. A shopper who doubts a purchase can weigh it there and report any shortage to the market office. The office then checks the vendor's scale, and repeat offenders may lose their stall permit. In the first month, the office received many reports, mostly about fish and meat stalls. After that, the number of reports dropped steadily. The administrator believes that most vendors adjusted their scales once they knew shoppers could check. Several honest vendors have welcomed the public scale, saying it protects their reputation. One fish vendor now invites doubtful customers to weigh their fish at the public scale before paying.

According to the passage, what may happen to repeat offenders?

- (A) They are fined twice the value of the goods
- (B) They must give free goods to shoppers
- (C) They may lose their stall permit
- (D) They are moved to the entrance

In response, the market administrator set up a "timbangan ng bayan," a public scale near the entrance that anyone can use for free. A shopper who doubts a purchase can weigh it there and report any shortage to the market office. The office then checks the vendor's scale, and repeat offenders may lose their stall permit. In the first month, the office received many reports, mostly about fish and meat stalls. After that, the number of reports dropped steadily. The administrator believes that most vendors adjusted their scales once they knew shoppers could check. Several honest vendors have welcomed the public scale, saying it protects their reputation. One fish vendor now invites doubtful customers to weigh their fish at the public scale before paying.

As used in the passage, the word "doubtful" most nearly means

- (A) unlikely
- (B) dishonest
- (C) certain
- (D) unsure

An alternative learning system (ALS) center in Cebu City holds classes from six to eight in the evening for adults who did not finish high school. The center uses two classrooms of a public elementary school, which lends them after the day's classes end. Most learners work during the day as vendors, drivers or household helpers. The teachers know that their learners are often tired, so each class begins with a short discussion of a news item before moving to lessons. Teachers also allow learners to bring their young children, who play quietly in a corner with donated toys. ### 33. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-101`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Water refilling stations have spread quickly in many towns, offering drinking water at a lower price than bottled water. For many families, a weekly delivery of refilled water has become as routine as buying rice. Because these stations are small businesses, they are inspected by the local health office. Inspectors take water samples every month and test them for bacteria. A station that fails a test must stop selling until it cleans its equipment and passes a second test. Health officers say most failures come from dirty containers rather than from the machines. Customers often bring their own containers, which may not be washed properly at home. For this reason, many stations now sell sealed containers that they clean and sanitize themselves. Health officers also advise customers to check that a station displays its latest water test certificate. A station that cannot show a recent certificate may not have been inspected, and customers have the right to ask.

- (D) How bacteria grow in water

A high school in Davao turned a waste problem into an art project. The project began almost by accident, when the teacher saw the canteen's garbage piled behind the gym. Tree-planting activities are popular with schools, offices and companies, but foresters warn that planting is only the first step. - (D) Native species grow faster than others
